newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber softens in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber softens in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices softened in dull late trading on Thursday on continued poor consumer demand, traders said.
They said offer prices for the benchmark SIR20 for April/May shipment slid to 51.75 U.S. cents/lb following fresh deals in Pontianak and Jambi, down from 52.00 in the morning.
Levels were generally stable at 52.50 fob Medan, at 52.375 fob Surabaya and at 52.125 fob Padang. Offer prices were slightly higher in Palembang at 52.75 fob.
Traders said they had expected offer prices to continue falling because of the absence of buyers.
"The market is lethargic because buyers are hiding themselves. Prices may fall to as low as 50.00 U.S. cents/lb someday and it's a pity," said one trader.
Some traders said they believed buyers had turned to Thailand because of the cheaper prices there and also to Vietnam which had started to sell rubber.
Traders said another factor which kept pushing the prices down was the ample supply in Indonesia despite wintering period in certain areas such as Aceh on Sumatra island.
"I don't think there is a problem with supply here because wintering period is only on certain areas," said one trader.
Traders said the market generally ignored the development in the Tokyo market lately because the movement there only dealt with ups and downs in the yen and dollar.
Tokyo rubber futures ended lower across the board on Thursday on technical-driven selling by private investors, stimulated by the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar.
Some Indonesian traders said demand was thin because main buyers in the U.S. and Europe, had already enough stocks.
